entities.name: Roger Bigod, 4th Earl of Norfolk
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Roger Bigod, 4th Earl of Norfolk (born unknown, died 1270-07-04), played a pivotal role in the 13th-century politics of England, serving as Marshal of England under King Henry III and King Edward I.

He was instrumental in the establishment of the English wool trade, a significant factor in the development of the country's economy during the medieval period.

As a key figure in the governance of Norfolk, a county in eastern England, Bigod worked closely with local nobles and clergy to maintain order and collect taxes.

The legacy of Roger Bigod, 4th Earl of Norfolk, can be seen in the continued importance of the wool trade in the region, as well as the enduring impact of his military campaigns on the politics of the region.

'War is a game of numbers,' Bigod once said, 'and I have played my part in shaping the fate of England.'
